transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net accounts and billing, my name is Oscar. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Oscar. I received an automated email this morning saying my monthly broadband direct debit failed and that I have a ten-pound late payment fee on my account, but I just switched bank accounts and set up the new details weeks ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your concern regarding the failed direct debit notification and the late fee, James. Let me look into your account ledger and sort this out for you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Oscar. I've always paid on time for four years, so seeing a late fee and threat of restriction was quite alarming.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To locate your billing profile on my screen, James, could you confirm the registered email on the account and your S-Net broadband account number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, the email is james.mitchell@outlook.com and my account number is SNET-839201.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the sort code of the new bank account you registered?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The new sort code is 40-22-18 with HSBC.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for providing those details, James. I have your billing file open.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what has occurred: you switched bank accounts to HSBC and submitted your new direct debit details, but your payment failed to collect yesterday, resulting in an automated ten-pound late payment surcharge on your statement. Have I understood correctly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. My bank said the Current Account Switch Service transfers all direct debits automatically, so I don't know why it bounced.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Checking the direct debit mandate logs... the automated mandate request was submitted to BACS on the first of the month, but your previous bank returned an R01 instruction saying account closed before the new mandate had fully originated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, so the old bank rejected the debit because the switch completed two days earlier than expected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. The timing overlapped by 48 hours, so BACS flagged the direct debit as rejected by paying bank.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you waive that ten-pound late payment fee since it was caused by the banking switch timing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. Because you used the official Current Account Switch Service and notified us in advance, that ten-pound fee was generated in error and I will remove it immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is brilliant, thank you Oscar. That's very fair.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's verify your new bank details so we can re-lodge the direct debit mandate correctly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I have my new debit card and account details right here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What is the eight-digit account number on your HSBC account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The account number is 74192834.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And the full name on the account as it appears on your bank statement?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's James Mitchell.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And would you prefer your monthly payment collection date to remain on the fourth of each month, or change to a different day?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could we change the payment date to the twenty-eighth of each month? That's when my salary is paid into the account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, moving your billing cycle to the twenty-eighth will align perfectly with your payday and prevent any cashflow issues.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would be so much better for our household budgeting.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If the 28th falls on a weekend or a bank holiday, when does BACS process the direct debit collection?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under direct debit rules, if your scheduled payment date lands on a Saturday, Sunday, or bank holiday, BACS automatically requests the debit on the very next working business day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So my account won't be charged early on a Friday before payday?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Never early, James. Payments are only ever collected on or after your designated billing date, never before.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That protects me from any unexpected overdraft charges over bank holiday weekends.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's process the outstanding monthly balance of forty-two pounds for this month so your broadband service remains completely active.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I pay that forty-two pounds right now over the phone with my debit card?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can take that card payment securely through our automated payment IVR system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let's do that right now so the balance is completely clear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I set up the secure payment portal and waive the fee.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, James. I have removed the ten-pound late fee and transferred you to the secure card payment portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I just entered my card details and the voice confirmed forty-two pounds payment accepted.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Checking the payment gateway... yes, authorization code 59281 confirms the forty-two pounds payment has cleared and your account balance is exactly zero pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is such a relief to have that sorted out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also submitted the new direct debit mandate to BACS for your HSBC account ending in 2834 with the new collection date of the 28th.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When will the next direct debit be collected then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your next payment will not be taken until the 28th of next month, giving you a full month of clear billing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fantastic. And there won't be any marks on my credit file for this failed attempt?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Zero marks whatsoever, James. Because the fee was waived and the balance cleared within 48 hours, no credit bureau reporting occurs.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That was my biggest worry with buying a house next year.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are completely protected under the Direct Debit Guarantee and our billing charter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will I receive an email confirmation of the updated mandate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, BACS requires a ten-day advance notice letter, which will be dispatched to your registered email within twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does the notice confirm the twenty-eighth payment date?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It confirms the exact collection schedule, your sort code, account number, and the monthly recurring charge of forty-two pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very clear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Would you also like me to set up an automated SMS alert three days prior to each payment collection?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, an SMS reminder on the twenty-fifth is very helpful to make sure funds are ready.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have enabled pre-collection payment SMS reminders on your mobile profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I view the status of the new direct debit mandate in the My S-Net mobile app right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, in the My S-Net mobile app under the Billing and Payments tab, your new HSBC mandate will show as Pending BACS Registration until tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And once BACS approves it tomorrow morning, the status updates to Active Mandate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Precisely. The badge turns green with Active Direct Debit, confirming all future collections will pull seamlessly on the twenty-eighth.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I set up a secondary backup payment method like a credit card just in case a future direct debit ever has an issue?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, our portal allows you to register a continuous payment authority on a backup debit or credit card that only activates if BACS returns an unpaid instruction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an excellent feature that prevents accidental late fees forever.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It ensures your broadband service never experiences temporary restrictions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me total peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oscar, you have handled this with complete professionalism. You explained the bank switch overlap, waived the fee, and moved my payment date.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure helping you today, James. Is there anything else regarding your broadband account that I can assist with?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, everything is completely resolved. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, James. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Oscar, goodbye.
